newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen rising, low bond yields to help.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen rising, low bond yields to help.

text.p: Stocks are expected to rise further on Tuesday, helped by falling bond yields and continued hopes for benefits from a rising yen to the dollar, brokers said.
On Monday, the composite index rallied 2.12 percent, or 14.95 points, to close at a three-month high of 721.20.
"The situation surrounding the market will remain brisk or improve," said Kim Ik-hwan, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Brokers said Monday's news that Midopa Department Store and three others of the Dainong Group's affiliates, would be bailed out would continue to be ignored.
The other three are textile maker Dainong Corp and two unlisted companies. Trading in Midopa and Dainong have been suspended from Monday afternoon.
As of the end of 1996, the group had 1.84 trillion won in debts, of which 86 percent was accounted for the four firms.
The three-year corporate yields closed at 12.15 percent on Monday, compared with as high as 12.33 percent a week before.
